Residual rank-invariance emerges when situational variability is constrained. In the context of team performance metrics like EPA, adjusting for situational factors such as down, distance, and field position results in minimal inter-team variation. As shown in the data, the standard deviation of these variables across teams is less than 2%, meaning that any residual adjustment is effectively a constant shift. This leads to a Pearson correlation of 1.000, indicating no reordering. The failure to reorder is not due to model misspecification but to the inherent structure of the data. Context-adjusted EPA is constructed to be rank-invariant by design, not because of weak modeling. The key insight is that when the variance in situational variables is negligible, the residual term becomes a near-constant across teams, eliminating any meaningful reordering effect. Thus, the metric fails to distinguish between teams beyond their inherent quality, which aligns with the observed positive correlation between situation mix and team quality. This reveals a fundamental duality: the metric is robust to situational noise but lacks sensitivity to dynamic changes in game context.
